Buy a Passport via Telegram: how the transaction works

Most Norwegian passport sellers work through a channel that posts stock and a chat that closes the sale. The channel is marketing. The chat is where you find out whether the person knows the document.

Keep the photos the seller sends. When the parcel arrives, photograph the unopened envelope before you open it, then the document beside the envelope. That sequence ties the document to the seller.

Who actually issues a Passport

The Norwegian passport is a state product made by the Politiet. Replicas copy the look, registered originals carry a number in the office records, and both are sold on Telegram as if they were the same thing.

Number formats are the one part of this that a buyer can always test without equipment. Look up the format for Norway and compare digit by digit. It takes a minute and settles most arguments.

Replica or registered original

A registered original is a document whose number sits in the office records. It may still be a genuine book with your details typed in, but the number resolves, and that is the whole difference in value.

That is why the number should be requested before any payment. If a seller sends the number first and invites you to check it, you are talking to somebody confident about the register.

What a fair price looks like

Price is the easiest thing to compare and the least informative. Two adverts at the same figure can differ completely in stock, number and delivery, and the figure shows you none of it.

The table below splits the band into the three tiers so you can see what each figure is actually for. Read it before you open a chat and you will not anchor on whatever number the seller opens with.

The buying process, step by step

The sequence below is the one that keeps you protected. Run it in order and do not skip ahead to payment.

  1. Ask which office issued it and confirm the answer is the Politiet.
  2. Request an uncropped photo of the full card on a plain surface with the laminate edge in frame.
  3. Request a UV shot of the data page and a close crop of the number field.
  4. Test the number against the format the Politiet uses. A number that breaks the format ends the deal.
  5. Agree a price inside the 1850–6300 NOK band and pay in two parts, deposit then balance against tracking.
  6. On arrival check the document against the photos before you accept delivery and photograph the unopened envelope.

Checks that catch bad stock

Run these before money moves. Each one targets a feature that survives handling but not a photocopier.

  • Check the licence for the Statens vegvesen mark and the two part category layout.
  • Confirm the passport crest and the eleven digit national identity number checksum.
  • Check the number format against the published rule for the Politiet. Constructed numbers cannot be invented by hand.
  • Look for the UV print with a 365 nanometre torch. Real ink is sharp and placed deliberately. A print shows a dull bloom or nothing.
  • Loupe the microprint and the ghost image. Both collapse into a dotted line or a grey patch on a photocopy.
  • Compare the data across every field for internal consistency. A postcode that contradicts the state or the office area is a tell.
  • Check the laminate or polycarbonate edge for a fused seal rather than a cut line under a laid sheet.

Red flags that should end the conversation

None of these are fatal alone. All of them are fatal when the seller has no explanation.

  • A document with a national identity number that fails both checksum digits.
  • The seller cannot name the issuing office, only the country.
  • The number breaks the published format, or is round and repeating.

Frequently asked questions

What should a passport cost on Telegram?

Between 180 and 900 US dollars depending on whether you are buying a print, correct stock, or a number that resolves at the issuing office.

Is a Telegram passport genuine?

Usually not. Most adverts sell a replica or a registered original, and the two are priced very differently. Ask which one it is in writing.

How long does delivery take?

Adverts quote anything from same day to four weeks. A tracked number that moves inside 48 hours is the realistic standard.

Can a passport number be checked?

Only against the issuing office register or an airline check-in system. A seller who offers no route to a register check is selling a print.

What is the most common fake?

A colour photocopy of a real data page laminated into a blank cover with a plausible number typed in.

Before you pay

Take the checks above into the chat. If a seller passes all of them, the Norwegian passport is worth the top of the band.
